notes.title: Rubbish Dump #5: Crafting & Resources Overhall
notes.content:
[h1]Hello Our Garbage People![/h1]

[h3]I’m [b]Hayley[/b], one of the programmers helping to bring trash to life, and I’m here with a slightly late but exciting rubbish dump! Last week was a busy one as we were frantically bug fixing and polishing the latest version of trash to showcase at the ACMI audience lab over the weekend. One of the new features we managed to get back in the game was our crafting system![/h3]

Crafting and resource collecting is going to be a big part of the gameplay experience in the final version of Trash so we wanted to get it back into the game for players to try as soon as we could. The premise is: in order to craft the forms that players will use to navigate the world of trash, they will need to first find and collect certain resources, then take them to the friendly crafting creatures who will help you create them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/92443ce9f681d6127abf2701815914f2abe00ed3.gif[/img]

As players progress, new resources will be discovered which in turn, allows players to craft different types of forms. In multiplayer games, forms crafted and resources collected will be shared amongst all players, so you can work together to solve puzzles and discover new places together!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/4a5db99ef77003d3a97f672e5c802e2bee623a0a.gif[/img]

It was a challenge to have to update the very old, demo versions of the inventory and crafting system code to work with our newer systems but I’m very glad I managed it without having to start from scratch! Plus seeing the creatures finally work in game, especially when we implemented Yee’s super cute animations, was so rewarding and fun!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/49b10f8193b49610dc750dec87ef6745c949213b.gif[/img]

[h3]I hope you enjoyed my garbage talk, watch this space for more updates from the rest of the team at Bin Chicken as we continue to work on “Trash” and bring our vision to life! [/h3]

tags.feature: One of the new features we managed to get back in the game was our crafting system!

notes.title: Rubbish Dump #4: ACMI Audience Lab
notes.content:
[h1]Hello Our Garbage People![/h1]

[h3]This weekend we spent two days with the public and a few other game developers here in rainy Melbourne in a lovely space, the Swinburne Studio at ACMI. The museum had invited us to participate in their Audience Lab event which brings together games, film and other screen media in development for playtesting with visitors! [/h3]

It was a great opportunity to get our work on the game into a playable state and we are really proud of a number of the new additions like upgradable world features that work with the reworked resources, the Cradle area which acts as a kind of hub, the new game intro cinematic, the new Turbine Challenge Element and a huge amount of work on the visual effects and lighting throughout the game. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/dc64c6dd39695f11c363a356fceea536d63a3a65.jpg[/img]

We are delighted that players had a lot of fun with some of the improvements we’ve made to existing parts of the game since we last playtested. The new movement mechanics for the Boulder Ball ability went down particularly well, as did the discovery and collection of resources.

For those of you who might be wondering, we don’t plan to bring out another playable demo so you’ll have to keep paying attention to these updates if you want to see the ongoing progress of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/ff1c5e9e2686f0d85ea24fc8d73c322b141d08c7.jpg[/img]

[h3]Thankyou to everyone who came along to the ACMI Audience Lab event on the weekend, it was a lot of fun![/h3]

notes.title: Rubbish Dump #3: Making New Hazard VFX
notes.content:
[h1]Hello Our Garbage People![/h1]


[h3]This is [b]Seb[/b] speaking! I'm a Technical artist at Bin chicken studios and I'm here to share with you a kinda pretty but also slightly dangerous update on the Hazardous areas of Trash! [/h3]

We've been hard at work to get the hazard system in the challenge zones looking and feeling awesome, today I'm going to give you a quick overview of what to expect from this system and how it will affect your time in the world of Trash. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/254969a9cb82658a2c00dff322e5875ee488a99c.gif[/img]

[h3]So for a quick overview of what the system is:[/h3]

While you are delving into the dangerous challenge zones by yourself or with some pals, you will come across a variety of different environmental hazards blocking your path. At this stage, we have implemented the first two sets of hazards which are fire or toxic based. These hazards will test your ability to navigate the space with varying degrees of difficulty, the challenges could include a ducting vent filled with gases igniting and releasing a torrent of flames, or a literal waterfall and river of toxic waste! It's going to be up to you to establish the best path forward or sometimes decide if it's worth the risk to get to scale the various puzzles for extra rewards!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/ad57eca89e2f3bd17b849cd2eb438fea03a49bcc.gif[/img]

Its been a blast working on these initial Hazard types and there several more to come so stay tuned! I hope you enjoyed my garbage talk, watch this space for more updates from the rest of the team at Bin Chicken as we continue to work on “Trash” and bring our vision to life! And for those of you in Melbourne, mark your calendars for May 6th and 7th to join in on the public testing in person at ACMI!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/df127e18f8b24ace8e820e7323fd853ad9aca34f.gif[/img]

[h2][h3]You can keep an eye on the [b]Audience Lab[/b] page here and sign up for emails to be notified when the event info goes live:[/h3][/h2]

[h3][h2][url=https://www.acmi.net.au/whats-on/acmi-rmit-audience-lab/]ACMI Audience Lab[/url][/h2][/h3]

notes.title: Taking Out The Trash - Demo Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/8afd068b2737314dd939ebbf1d8ae8c9c90d93fa.png[/img]

[h3][b]First, a thank you![/b][/h3]

Thanks so much to all our fans and players out there who played Trash’s early [b]Public Alpha Demo[/b] and gave us such helpful and wonderful feedback! After the release of [b]Trash’s Holiday Update[/b], we took a brief dev holiday ourselves in order to refresh our wasted brains (our creative director was starting to wonder whether he was in fact himself, a trash based life form). Since returning we have spent a number of months looking over all the feedback and finding ways we can improve the demo before we move towards our next stage of development. 

[h3][b]What is this trash all about?[/b][/h3]

[b]The Taking Out The Trash Update[/b] isn’t a content update, rather a chance for us to add the things you asked for and make Trash easier to pick up and play! The update aims to improve player experience and give you your friends a funner, trashier time! As always the demo can be played either solo or cooperatively online with up to 3 friends!

[h3][b]A Rubbish List of Changes[/b][/h3]

[b]UI[/b]
[*] New player objective system
[*] New Resource pickup notifications
[*] New ingame directional signs 
[*] New player interactions
[*] Improved UI visuals & designs
[*] Improved & simplified  ingame language
[*] Updated Splash Screens & Menu Layout

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/f4834535897047b80fc158263712cb37640e80bc.gif[/img]

[b]Player Character[/b]
[*] New player form VFX
[*] New player resource pickups zones
[*] New player form use opportunities
[*] Improved player interaction mechanics
[*] Improved player camera mechanics
[*] Improved player movement and jump mechanics

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/79d254e4958df6367e62f9a305f85989aae8947d.gif[/img]

[b]Cinematics[/b]
[*] New internal Challenge Zone cinematic cameras 
[*] New external Challenge Zone cinematic cameras
[*] New game progression cinematic cameras
[*] Improved cinematic demo ending

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/fe654818e093a69c11d616d04a03dccb29bf588e.gif[/img]

[b]Environment[/b]
[*] Improved object & environment colliders
[*] Improved player start zone
[*] Improved resource VFX
[*] Improved Challenge Zone visuals and decals

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/32ce2e2af6dc507ae8d4c88f33a64019a0594437.gif[/img]

[b]Optimisation[/b]
[*] New Flora LOD system
[*] New graphics and resolution settings

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/4fea9cb0bb5ada8178a863ac812ebd96a9e3328d.gif[/img]

[b]Audio[/b]
[*] Objective complete fanfare 
[*] Audio zones for environmental VFX



[h3]We appreciate your support & hope you find the time to give Trash a play! If you do, you can give us feedback here:[/h3]

[url=https://twitter.com/15MinutesOfGame]Twitter[/url]
[url=https://forms.gle/DNLSHqA3FQ3BJQ4e6]Feedback Form[/url]
or in our community page!

[h3]Have a rubbish day! [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305017/e3a301374c532bb0ad7c6e2eede18625d8802965.jpg[/img]

[h3]And now, a massive list of fixed bugs![/h3]

[b]Resources Bugs[/b]

[*] Client: Challenge Zone resource collection error ResourceManager.DestroyResourceObject
[*] Client: pickup resource incorrect tally in UI
[*] Client: picking up resource while host is in menu (in-game) doesn’t update inventory counts

[b]Challenge Zones (CZ's) Bugs[/b]

[*] CZ6 state 2 triggers when CZ5 completed
